payload.purpose_context: Core side of spec-kitty-charter ADR-0013 (#62 #63 #64 #66 #67). Today deactivation only removes an id from an allow-list, raises when the list is absent, and is undone by cascade, upgrade resets and org required_* unions. A new .kittify/charter/activation.yaml becomes the single authority for activated_<kind> and deactivated_<kind>; cascade skips and reports excluded nodes; deactivating a required artifact is refused naming the org pack.
payload.purpose_tldr: A deactivated charter element stays gone: one activation ledger holds allow and deny state, and cascade, upgrade and presets honour it.

payload.question: Core has no charter-activation conformance corpus (spec-kitty-charter #9 open, export script unwritten). What does 'regenerate the corpus' mean here?

payload.final_answer: The conformance corpus lives inside the migrated/ported test cases and the open-packs content: write the fixed answers as portable, data-driven acceptance cases; no separate export script.

payload.question: Moving activated_* out of charter.yaml widens activation under an older CLI (absent = all). How to handle?

payload.final_answer: Move the keys out (activation.yaml is the only authority); document the downgrade hazard in changelog Upgrade Notes and the ADR; doctor flags activation keys that reappear in charter.yaml/config.yaml.

payload.question: How does the new CLI behave on a project with legacy activated_* and no activation.yaml (pre-upgrade)?

payload.final_answer: A migration run is added, so the upgrade takes care of it: the ledger is read only from activation.yaml, no runtime legacy fallback; test fixtures are re-seeded into activation.yaml.

payload.question: Where do allow and deny state live? (operator ruling in the mission brief)

payload.final_answer: New .kittify/charter/activation.yaml is the single authority for activated_<kind> (three-state) and deactivated_<kind> deny-lists; effective = allow (or all) minus deny; empty deny-lists omitted; other surfaces derive from it and doctor reports divergence.

payload.question: How does the activation seam behave before the ledger migration has run (shipped migrations write through it during an upgrade)?

payload.final_answer: Upgrade-only legacy, else refuse: ledger present -> ledger only; legacy keys and no ledger -> ordinary CLI commands fail closed (ActiveCharterConfigError, 'run spec-kitty upgrade'), while inside the upgrade runner the seam keeps targeting the legacy surface so shipped migrations behave as today until the ledger migration moves the keys; no legacy keys -> ledger.

payload.question: Which write paths may change a deny-list?

payload.final_answer: Presets with --force too: only charter activate <kind> <id> (incl. --only), a cascade with --include-deactivated, and charter activate --preset X --force (for ids the preset lists, reported) clear deny entries. Presets without --force, the interview and every other writer never touch deny keys; a denied id they list stays subtracted with a warning. Ids dropped by --only narrowing get no deny entry.

payload.question: Does a cascade activation walk continue through a deactivated node to its children?

payload.final_answer: Stop at the denied node: nothing reachable only through it is activated; children reachable over another non-excluded path still are; --include-deactivated restores the full walk.

payload.question: Leftover config.yaml copy holds a key the authoritative charter.yaml lacks: what does the ledger migration do?

payload.final_answer: Refuse as divergent: name the key and both files, change nothing.
